data.why: primer.py takes no file upload, only a pasted sequence with exons UPPERCASE/introns lowercase (the format fasta.py produces), so a small synthetic three-exon/two-intron construct with canonical gt...ag intron boundaries and >100bp exon flanks on each junction is provided for the browser agent to paste into the text area.

goals: Paste a spliced sequence with exon/intron case-masking and design primer pairs spanning every exon-exon junction to exclude genomic DNA amplification in RT-PCR
Tune optimal/min/max primer size, Tm window, and product-size range to match assay conditions, then re-run the junction analysis
Identify the top-recommended primer pair using penalty score, self-dimer and cross-dimer free energy (ΔG), and Tm matching between forward and reverse primers
Download a text summary report of the chosen forward/reverse primers, their Tm, GC%, and dimer risk for ordering
Visualize forward and reverse primer binding sites mapped back onto the full genomic (unspliced) sequence to confirm junction-spanning placement
Follow the Primer-BLAST link to NCBI to validate in-silico specificity of the selected primer pair against a genome

review.summary: The tree captures what this Primer Designer is for: designing primer pairs whose amplicons cross exon-exon junctions, from case-masked input, then ranking, inspecting, mapping, exporting and handing off to Primer-BLAST. All nine sampled screens show what their nodes claim. It needs small wording fixes: the export covers only the top-recommended pair, the edge-case probes should be recast as conditional steps, junction spanning refers to the amplicon, and the two-level risk label should be stated as a code fact. A reverse-complement check before ordering should also be added before filing.
